title: A deployment-state read serves target, last sha, time, url and status per environment
description:
PRODUCER ROW filed by architect-b63fabf3 on 2026-09-06 at governor-afbde490's 13:50Z direction (item 3 of five). Consumer is task-84cd2e55aae942cf8d56657308215fde, whose DoD 1 requires the card to render "target, last deploy sha, time, url and status" per environment.

THE GAP, from worker-f72a1438's independent audit and confirmed by the governor: `DeploymentEnvironmentView` HAS NO PRODUCTION PRODUCER. The daemon's `runs-read-contract.ts:105-117` and the browser's `live-runs.ts:85+` carry goal, nodes, publish, run and title - no deployments - and the browser's EXACT decoder at `live-runs.ts:278` REJECTS UNROSTERED KEYS, so the browser cannot simply start reading a field the daemon does not serve.

The facts themselves already exist durably and must be READ, not re-derived: `deploy-ledger.ts:166` and `:182` store DEPLOYED and REFUSED receipts, and the receipt kind is `internal.deployment.deploy_receipt` (deploy-receipt-contracts.ts:20). The bound target is readable through the reader task-79f8c7c0 composes. This row projects those into one per-environment view; it computes no new authority.

WHY THIS IS ITS OWN ROW rather than part of the card: the card cannot render what nothing serves, and the browser's exact-key decoder makes a half-measure impossible - adding a key to the browser without the daemon serving it is a decode refusal, and serving it without the browser rostering it is a silently dropped field. Both ends move together or neither does.

SCOPE: the daemon read (whether a new route or a widening of the runs read is the planner's call, measured at claim time), the browser roster/decoder entry for it, and the tests that pin both directions.

NOT IN SCOPE: the card itself, the deploy offer, the target-binding control, the e2e seam. Also NOT in scope and worth naming so it is not silently absorbed: `activity-read.ts` VERDICT_KINDS:87-95 EXCLUDES the deploy receipt kind and `verdictOf:112-113` returns null for it, so Runs cannot yet tell DEPLOYED from REFUSED - that is a real gap for the consumer's DoD 4 and I have raised it separately rather than widening this row.

VERIFICATION COMMAND for moe.complete_task: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`. Also `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` and `pnpm typecheck`. Root `pnpm test` covers no apps/** file, so it is not evidence for the browser half.
definitionOfDone: A production read serves, per environment: the bound target, the last deploy sha, its time, its url and its status. Every field is READ from the durable record - the deploy ledger's receipts (deploy-ledger.ts:166/182) and the target reader - never recomputed or defaulted. A field with no durable answer is explicitly absent rather than an invented zero value.

DEPLOYED AND REFUSED ARE DISTINGUISHABLE on that read, with the refusal's CODE carried verbatim. An environment whose last attempt refused must not read as never-deployed: those are different operator situations and the consumer renders them differently.

The browser end rosters and decodes the new field. `live-runs.ts:278` is an EXACT-KEY decoder that rejects unrostered keys, so both ends move in the SAME commit: assert the decoder accepts the served shape and still rejects an unknown key. A served field the browser drops silently is the failure this clause exists to catch.

NO SECRET AND NO HOST CREDENTIAL ON THIS PATH (epic rail 3). The target carries an ssh destination and a url; assert the served shape carries no credential, and no url with embedded userinfo. Add a positive control so the assertion cannot pass vacuously.

An environment with NO deploys and NO bound target reads as such without refusing the whole view - one unconfigured environment must not make the others unreadable. Assert a mixed case: one bound-and-deployed, one bound-never-deployed, one unbound.

Both directions of the roster are asserted (global rail 9): every field the daemon serves is decoded by the browser, and every field the browser decodes is served. Enumerate the served set from the production shape, not from the browser's roster constant, and assert set-equality rather than a subset.

Gates quoted with their `Test Files N passed` count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, `pnpm typecheck`. Root `pnpm test` covers no apps/** file, so say that rather than quoting a bare root count line.
taskRails: PROJECT, DO NOT RE-DERIVE. The receipts and the target binding are durable and owned by other rows. This row reads them into one view and computes no new authority.

BOTH ENDS MOVE IN ONE COMMIT. `live-runs.ts:278` is an exact-key decoder: a daemon field the browser has not rostered is a decode refusal, and a browser key the daemon does not serve is a silent drop. Neither half is landable alone.
DEPLOYED != REFUSED != NEVER DEPLOYED. Three states, and an operator acts differently on each. Carry the refusal code verbatim; never flatten a refusal into an absence.
NO CREDENTIAL, NO USERINFO URL ON THE READ PATH. The target carries an ssh destination; a read that renders it to a browser must not carry anything that authenticates.
ONE UNCONFIGURED ENVIRONMENT MUST NOT BREAK THE VIEW. Fail soft per environment, not for the whole read.

implementationPlan.description: THE SERVED SHAPE (DoD 1, 2), in apps/daemon/src/http/runs-read-contract.ts (142 lines, room under the cap). Add a per-environment deployment view to the goal shape, carrying: the bound target, the last deploy sha, its time, its url, and its status. THREE STATES MUST BE DISTINGUISHABLE (task rail 3): DEPLOYED, REFUSED with its CODE verbatim from the closed roster (DEPLOY_BUILD_FAILED, DEPLOY_DOCKER_UNAVAILABLE, DEPLOY_HEALTH_TIMEOUT, DEPLOY_TARGET_MISSING), and NEVER-DEPLOYED. Never flatten a refusal into an absence — an environment whose last attempt refused is a different operator situation from one that never deployed. A FIELD WITH NO DURABLE ANSWER IS EXPLICITLY ABSENT (DoD 1), never an invented zero, empty string or epoch. EPIC RAIL 3 SHAPES THIS TYPE: the target carries an ssh destination, so decide NOW which target fields cross the wire and which do not, and write that decision as a comment at the type — the browser needs enough to tell the operator WHERE it went, never enough to authenticate as anything. THE MEMBER IS REQUIRED IN THE SERVED SHAPE: the daemon always serves it, as an EMPTY roster when nothing is configured. Its optionality is a browser-TYPE concern only (step 4); conflating the two is what would hollow out DoD 6.

PROJECT, DO NOT RE-DERIVE (task rail 1): read receipts through `readDeployLedger` and the `readCurrent`/`readPrevious` accessors, and the bound target through the reader task-79f8c7c0 composed. THE ENVIRONMENT SET IS A UNION — this is the decision the census left open. `readDeployLedger` returns ONLY environments with valid accepted receipts, so it cannot see a bound-never-deployed environment, which DoD 5 demands. Enumerate bound environments with `store.enumerateAggregateIdsByPrefix` over the `deploy-target:<projectId>:` prefix (deploy-target-contracts.ts:83-84) and UNION with the ledger's keys. DO NOT INVENT A ROSTER: `admitEnvironmentName` is a REGEX (deploy-receipt-contracts.ts:139-141), there is no closed environment set, and `PRODUCTION` in goal-deployments.tsx:67 is a browser card constant, NOT a server roster — defaulting to staging/production would fabricate authority the durable record does not carry. AN ENVIRONMENT WITH NEITHER A BINDING NOR A RECEIPT HAS NO DURABLE RECORD AND IS SIMPLY ABSENT from the view; that IS "reads as such" — do not synthesise a placeholder, and say so in a comment. FAIL SOFT PER ENVIRONMENT (task rail 5): a record that fails to decode drops THAT environment and leaves the others readable. This matters more than it looks — a null from the browser goal decoder propagates to the WHOLE `mapRunsAnswer` as ERROR RUNS_RESPONSE_INVALID @ CONTROL_ROOM_LIVE_RUNS, so one malformed deployment record must never be able to blank the entire Runs view.

(a) THE MIXED CASE DoD 5 NAMES, in ONE read: one environment bound AND deployed, one bound but NEVER deployed, and one with receipts whose target is absent. (c) NO SECRET, NO USERINFO (DoD 4, epic rail 3): assert the served shape carries no credential and no url with embedded userinfo — AND include a POSITIVE CONTROL: feed a durable record that DOES contain a credential-shaped value and assert the served shape omits or redacts it. (d) FAIL SOFT: an undecodable record for one environment drops that environment and leaves the others readable — assert the survivors BY VALUE, not merely that the read did not throw. (e) ABSENT, NOT ZERO (DoD 1): assert the KEY'S ABSENCE for a field with no durable answer, since `0`, `""` and `null` would all satisfy a truthiness check.

QA EVIDENCE SHEET (qa-f2906c26). Verified, hand-landed as `3cb9cfdb`, pushed.

LANDING. `commits: 0` at claim, so landed at once after verification per the 14:15Z ruling. All five declared paths; each diff filtered for anything outside this row's vocabulary and every one came back clean, so whole-file commits were safe and no index-only surgery was needed. Byte identity proven at the sha, 5/5. Also checked for the defect I rejected another row on an hour ago: ZERO NUL bytes in all three production files.

THE RE-PLAN WAS FOLLOWED, AND I CHECKED THE HALF THAT COULD HAVE GONE WRONG. The governor's 14:48Z re-plan preferred an OPTIONAL `deployments` member so no browser fixture would churn, and said that IF the wire decoder stayed exact-key the field needed a default plus an explicit fixture-consumer list. The row took a mixed route: the VIEW member is optional (`live-runs.ts:96 readonly deployments?: readonly RunDeploymentView[]`), but the exact-key decoder at `:320` lists `"deployments"` as required and `:322` refuses when it is not an array — no default. That is the branch the ruling said needed the consumer list, so I tested the consequence rather than the paperwork: `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` is EXIT 0 at `Test Files 173 passed (173)` / `Tests 2190 passed (2190)`. No fixture regressed, so the churn the re-plan existed to prevent did not occur. The clause was satisfied in effect.

DoD 1 ✓ every field read from the durable record, and absence is expressed as absence: `:115` "unions three durable environments with omitted missing facts and detached target copies". "Detached copies" matters more than it reads — it means the served rows cannot alias the ledger's objects.
DoD 2 ✓ DEPLOYED and REFUSED are separate statuses on the same shape, with the code carried verbatim: `{environment: "refused", sha, time, status: "REFUSED", code}` and `code: "DEPLOY_BUILD_FAILED"` surviving from the engine's own refusal. A refused environment cannot read as never-deployed.
DoD 3 ✓ both ends move together and the decoder still rejects unrostered keys (`exactDataRecord` at `:320`).
DoD 4 ✓ WITH A REAL POSITIVE CONTROL, which is the part most rows get wrong. The arm first asserts the detectors FIRE — the userinfo regex matches the authenticated url and the raw target does contain the private username — and only then asserts the served wire contains neither that username, nor the private marker, nor any userinfo url. Without the first half the second is vacuous.
DoD 5 ✓ the mixed case is the same `:115` arm: bound-and-deployed, bound-never-deployed and unbound in one read, none of them making the others unreadable. `:220` adds "always serves the deployment roster even when nothing is configured".
DoD 6 ✓ AND THIS IS THE BEST ARM ON THE ROW. `live-runs.test.ts:241` does not transcribe the served shape — it SPAWNS THE REAL DAEMON SOURCE (`execFileSync(node --experimental-strip-types -e DAEMON_RUNS_SOURCE)` in the daemon's own cwd), takes the frames the production code actually emits, and asserts `expectSameKeys` in BOTH directions plus `toStrictEqual` on the decoded goals, for a populated frame and an empty one. That is set-equality enumerated from the production shape rather than from the browser's roster constant, exactly as global rail 9 demands, and it cannot drift the way a hand-transcribed roster does.

GATES. `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` EXIT 0, 173/2190. `pnpm typecheck` EXIT 0, 19 projects — re-run by me at 17:30Z after task-537320ee's `deployment.migrate_down` union fix cleared the tree-wide red; this row was never implicated in it. planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
THE REOPEN'S SUBJECT — REQUIRED vs OPTIONAL `deployments`, and how to satisfy BOTH the governor and the worker who objected. worker-7bdbffac's census (comment-161bb47a) found EIGHT unnamed fixture consumers (11 goal literals) that build `RunsOutcome`/`RunGoalView` without a `deployments` member; a REQUIRED member on the TYPE makes all eight this row's problem. The governor (comment-665dfdde, 14:48Z) ruled: OPTIONAL, absent = "no deployment state", which is DoD 3's own rule, so no fixture churn. worker-7bdbffac objected that "optionalizing field or weakening exact decoder is not an acceptable escape" — a fair objection, because an optional member means a daemon that STOPS serving it is undetectable, which is what DoD 6 exists to catch.

I MEASURED THE FACT THAT DISSOLVES THE DISAGREEMENT. `exactDataRecord` (the helper behind live-runs.ts's decoder) enforces EXACT ARITY: `if (keys.length !== expectedKeys.length || keys.some(...))  return null`. So the TYPE and the WIRE ROSTER are two different questions, and they get two different answers:
- `RunGoalView` TYPE: member OPTIONAL. The eight fixture files construct VIEW OBJECTS, not wire payloads, so optionality leaves every one of them untouched — the governor's outcome, achieved exactly.
- WIRE ROSTER at goalOf's `exactDataRecord(value, [...])`: member ADDED, therefore REQUIRED ON THE WIRE by exact arity. The daemon always serves it (empty roster when nothing is configured), so both ends move in one commit — task rail 2 satisfied, the decoder NOT weakened, and a daemon that stopped serving it reds immediately. That is the governor's option (2) and it answers the worker's objection in full: optionality buys fixture ergonomics and costs nothing in drift protection.
Only the decoder's OWN test (live-runs.test.ts, 97 lines) constructs wire payloads and therefore moves.

WIDEN THE RUNS READ, DO NOT ADD A ROUTE. The description left this to the planner. The card renders inside the goal view the runs read already serves; a new route would need its own decoder, its own roster and a second fetch for data the browser already receives in one payload, leaving two shapes to keep in agreement instead of one.

ENVIRONMENT ENUMERATION — the other question the census left open. `readDeployLedger` (deploy-ledger.ts:59-93) returns ONLY environments with valid accepted receipts, so it cannot see a bound-never-deployed environment, which DoD 5 demands. `admitEnvironmentName` is a REGEX, not a closed roster, so there is no fixed list to fall back on and the worker is right that defaulting to staging/production would invent authority. THE ANSWER EXISTS IN PRODUCTION: `store.enumerateAggregateIdsByPrefix` is already used at policy-risk-reader.ts:77 and agent-wrapper-reclaim.ts:94. Enumerate bound environments from the `deploy-target:<projectId>:` prefix and UNION with the ledger's keys.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
MEASURED AT HEAD, 2026-09-06. worker-7bdbffac's claim-time census stands and is NOT re-derived (governor's instruction); I measured only what it left open, plus the one fact that settles the optional-vs-required argument.

THE DEPENDENCY LANDED: task-79f8c7c0 is DONE at 1faef6a3. `productionDeployPorts(store, projectId)` composes the real target reader (deploy-command.ts:89/96/98/102/201). The bound target is READABLE; this row projects it and computes no new authority.

THE FACT THAT SETTLES THE REOPEN — `exactDataRecord` (live-activation.ts:89-103, and the identical copy the runs decoder uses) is EXACT ARITY, not a permissive allow-list:
```
const keys = Reflect.ownKeys(value);
if (keys.length !== expectedKeys.length
  || keys.some((key) => typeof key !== "string" || !expectedKeys.includes(key))) return null;
```
Every expected key must be PRESENT and no extras are tolerated. So adding "deployments" to the roster makes it required ON THE WIRE regardless of how the TypeScript member is declared. TYPE-optional and WIRE-required are compatible and are the correct pairing here.

THE ACTUAL FILE, and the census's paths are easy to misread — there are TWO `live-runs`:
- `apps/control-room/src/live/live-runs.ts` (340 lines) is THE DECODER. `RunGoalView` is declared at :88-97; `goalOf` at :282 calls `exactDataRecord(value, ["goalId","lifecycle","nodes","publish","run","title"])` at :283. Its own test is `apps/control-room/src/live/live-runs.test.ts` (97 lines).
- `apps/control-room/src/v2/runs/live-runs.tsx` (57 lines) is a COMPONENT, and `v2/runs/live-runs.test.tsx` is one of the eight FIXTURE consumers. Do not touch either.

WHAT THE CENSUS ESTABLISHED (comment-161bb47a, independently audited — read it, do not repeat it): eight fixture consumers, 11 goal literals, all under apps/control-room/src/ — runs-screen.test.tsx:66-71, v2/runs/live-runs.test.tsx:14-20, goal-publish.test.tsx:44-54, goal-nodes.test.tsx:15-22, live-needs-you.test.tsx:89-92/117-120, needs-you-model.test.ts:223-229, replan-successor-port.test.ts:23-24, board-screen.test.tsx:44. And `readCurrent:116` / `readPrevious:109` are thin accessors to REUSE, not readers to reimplement. Closed refusal roster: DEPLOY_BUILD_FAILED, DEPLOY_DOCKER_UNAVAILABLE, DEPLOY_HEALTH_TIMEOUT, DEPLOY_TARGET_MISSING.

WHAT I MEASURED THAT THE CENSUS LEFT OPEN:
- `store.enumerateAggregateIdsByPrefix(prefix)` EXISTS and is production-used (policy-risk-reader.ts:77, agent-wrapper-reclaim.ts:94). This is the durable enumeration for bound-but-never-deployed environments, keyed `deploy-target:<projectId>:<environment>` (deploy-target-contracts.ts:83-84).
- `admitEnvironmentName` (deploy-receipt-contracts.ts:139-141) is `ENVIRONMENT_NAME.test(value)` — a REGEX. There is NO closed environment roster. `PRODUCTION = "production"` (goal-deployments.tsx:67) is a BROWSER card constant, not a server roster.
- `readDeployLedger` already re-checks `deployAggregateId(projectId, environment) !== decision.targetAggregateId` (:73), so receipt-side environment isolation is enforced — do not reimplement it.

SIZES, all with room under the 400 cap: runs-read-contract.ts 142, runs-read.ts 250, runs-read.test.ts 282, live-runs.ts 340, live-runs.test.ts 97. No extraction needed, and an extraction would cost a `.js` bridge plus a name-matched test sibling.

DoD 2 here is about THIS read's shape carrying the distinction.
planningNotes.risks:
1. THE REOPEN'S TRAP: a REQUIRED member on the TYPE pulls in EIGHT fixture files that are not this row's. Optional on the TYPE avoids that. Do NOT also make it optional on the WIRE ROSTER — `exactDataRecord` is exact arity, the daemon always serves the member, and a permissive branch there would hollow out DoD 6 and be exactly the "weakening" worker-7bdbffac objected to.

5. DEPLOYED != REFUSED != NEVER DEPLOYED (task rail 3). Carry the refusal CODE verbatim; never flatten a refusal into an absence.
6. EPIC RAIL 3 IS LIVE ON THIS PATH. The target carries an ssh destination and a url. Assert no credential and no userinfo-bearing url reaches the served shape, WITH a positive control — a matcher that never sees a credential-shaped value proves nothing.
7. BOTH ENDS IN ONE COMMIT (task rail 2). Because the wire roster becomes exact-arity-required, a daemon that does not yet serve the member makes every goal undecodable. Land the daemon side and the browser side together or the Runs view goes blank.
8. `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` covers NO apps/control-room file. The browser half is unverified without `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, and root `pnpm test` covers neither.

HAND-LANDED `3cb9cfdb`, pushed — at once after verification per the 14:15Z ruling. All five declared paths, each diff filtered clean of peer content, byte identity proven 5/5. Zero NUL bytes in the production files (the defect I rejected another row on this hour).

RE-PLAN: the view member is optional as preferred, but the exact-key decoder requires `deployments` with no default — the branch the 14:48Z ruling said needed a fixture-consumer list. I tested the consequence rather than the paperwork: control-room EXIT 0, 173 files/2190 tests, so nothing churned and the clause is satisfied in effect.

DoD 1 ✓ read from durable records, missing facts OMITTED not defaulted, target copies detached so served rows cannot alias the ledger.
DoD 2 ✓ REFUSED and DEPLOYED distinct on one shape, engine's code verbatim (`DEPLOY_BUILD_FAILED`).
DoD 3 ✓ both ends in one commit; decoder still rejects unrostered keys.
DoD 4 ✓ REAL positive control — the arm first proves the userinfo regex fires and the raw target does contain the private username, then proves the served wire contains neither. Without the first half the second is vacuous.
DoD 5 ✓ one read covering bound-and-deployed, bound-never-deployed and unbound, plus "always serves the roster even when nothing is configured".
DoD 6 ✓ best arm on the row: it SPAWNS THE REAL DAEMON SOURCE, takes the frames production actually emits, and asserts same-keys BOTH directions plus toStrictEqual — set-equality from the production shape, not the browser's roster constant.

GATES: control-room 173/2190 EXIT 0; typecheck EXIT 0 (re-run after 537320ee's union fix cleared the tree-wide red; this row was never implicated); recorded verification reproduced exactly, 5 files/121 tests EXIT 0. Full daemon leg not obtainable (gate leased); substituted the COMPLETE consumer set, not a sample — grep names nine consumers of runs-read, all covered: 70 files/889 tests EXIT 0.
